newsitem.title: POLAND: EU says Poland needs full adjustment to be member.
newsitem.headline: EU says Poland needs full adjustment to be member.

text.p: EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek on Friday warned Poland that it could not expect swift entry to the European Union unless it met all EU requirements.

Van den Broek told an international investor conference in Warsaw the transition of adjusting to EU standards in Poland was well advanced but the country still needed to make big adjustments to be ready for membership.

"No applicant country can afford to relax its reform efforts on the assumption that early membership is guaranteed on political grounds and that gaps in its legal structures or practices can be taken care of after accession through exceptions to rules, known as derogations," van den Broek said.
"New member states will be expected to accept...all the rights and obligations arising from EU treaties and legislation, as a whole, from the date of accession," he added.
Poland, now an EU associate member, hopes to become a full member around the year 2000. But the European Commission has signalled 2002 as a more realistic target.

Van den Broek said the major adjustments Poland had to make ranged from "the acceleration of privatisation to the reform of public administration, including civil control of all government departments."
He said in recent months Poland and the EU have run into a number of problems in sensitive sectors such as oil, the car industry and steel.
He said Poland was not ready to keep to the agreed calendar of lifting duties on EU steel on January 1, 1997, but that talks on a compromise solution were in progress.
"I am pleased that progress on some of these problems has been made during my present visit and trust that we can soon put them behind us and concentrate on preparations for membership," he said.
Van den Broek stressed the need for reform in the Polish banking sector saying it was vital to provide services for firms and to impose finncial discipline on them.

"The Polish banking sector needs root and branch reform, based on sound economic and financial analysis. The government faces a great challange in the coming years in privatising large parts of the banking sector which are under state control," he said.
Van den Broek criticised delays in the privatisation and restructuring of large state-owned companies for political and social reasons, which he called "short-term thinking".

"Many companies are virtually untouched by reform. There has been a tendency to postpone large-scale restructuring in some sectors because of its possible social and political ramifications," he said.

Van den Broek said the EU Commission had until mid-1997 to present a formal opinion to the EU's Council of Ministers on the 10 applications from Central and Eastern European and other countries it was reviewing.
"In these opinions we shall be looking at the capacity of the candidate country to implement effectively the rights and obligations which come with Union membership," he said.
